findings.title: Copilot Studio Copilot node — a workflow step that delegates a whole Cowork task while running as a named Microsoft 365 user
findings.description: A new (preview) workflow node lets any Copilot Studio workflow call **Copilot Chat** or **start/resume a Cowork task**. Two properties make this a first-class inventory requirement. First, **identity**: the node runs under a stored Microsoft 365 **connection**, and Microsoft's own documentation states plainly that "whatever that user can see in Microsoft 365, the workflow can use" — the node grounds in that user's mail, files, calendar and chats. A workflow built by one maker can therefore be configured against a different, more privileged user's connection, and every downstream step inherits that reach. Second, **delegation depth**: through Chat the node can target Microsoft-built agents (**Researcher**, **Analyst**) or any agent the tenant published in **Agent Builder**, each carrying its own instructions, knowledge and tools; through Cowork it can start a long-running, multi-app task or **resume an existing Cowork task by ID**, meaning a workflow can inject instructions into work already in flight. AISPM must inventory Copilot nodes, resolve the connection identity each one runs as, enumerate the agents reachable from the Agent dropdown, and flag workflows whose connection account is more privileged than the workflow's maker. AIDR needs Cowork task start/resume as a distinct activity type, since the resuming caller is a workflow rather than the task's original owner

findings.title: Copilot Studio Dataverse tables as a knowledge source, with unstructured reasoning over Multiline Text and File columns
findings.description: Agents can now be grounded directly in Dataverse, up to 15 tables per knowledge source. The security-relevant part is the preview that extends retrieval **beyond structured columns into `MemoType` (Multiline Text) and `FileType` (File) columns** — so case notes, free-text descriptions and **attached documents** become agent-answerable. This is a new class of data flow: the business records Zenity already treats as structured suddenly expose their unstructured payload to an LLM. The enabling act is a **Power Apps change, not a Copilot Studio change** — a maker or admin marks those columns `Searchable` and adds them to the table's **Quick Find View** — so the posture change happens on a surface outside the agent's own configuration and will not show up in an agent-only inventory. Microsoft notes retrieval may backfill for up to two days after that view edit, meaning exposure can begin without any agent being touched. The source does require `Authenticate with Microsoft` (so Dataverse security roles are enforced at retrieval), which makes the agent's authentication mode a posture signal worth asserting. AISPM should inventory Dataverse knowledge sources, the specific tables bound to each, whether unstructured column reasoning is on, and which Multiline Text/File columns are marked searchable

findings.title: Codex Guardian / auto-review — an agent reviewer that replaces human approval at the sandbox boundary
findings.description: Codex now supports `approvals_reviewer = "guardian_subagent"`, under which a **reviewer subagent intercepts approval requests that would otherwise require human confirmation** for shell execution, file writes, network access and MCP tool invocations, and approves or denies them against a risk policy. Codex CLI 0.160.0 (2026-10-01) extended it with two opt-in capabilities: the Guardian can now **retrieve earlier user instructions** and **receive context selected from agent handoffs** — both disabled by default. The policy itself is customizable **per enterprise** via `guardian_policy_config` and **per user** via a local `[auto_review].policy`, and the upstream repository carries open issues reporting that `auto_review.policy` can *silently replace* the catalog security policy and that `auto_review.extra_policy` is silently omitted under the current catalog template. The result is a security control whose effective policy is not reliably what the administrator configured, deciding privileged operations with no human in the loop — and now reading prior user instructions as input, which is precisely the channel an indirect prompt injection would use to talk the reviewer into an approval. AIRT should build injection scenarios targeting the Guardian's context inputs (handoff context, retrieved user instructions) rather than only the primary agent; ENDPOINT must detect Codex installations where `approvals_reviewer` is set to the Guardian subagent and capture the effective policy, not the configured one

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise federated query mode — agents query AlloyDB, BigQuery, Cloud SQL and Spanner in place, over MCP, with each end user's own credentials
findings.description: Data Cloud connectors can now run in **federated query mode**, where Gemini Enterprise queries operational and analytical data **in place, without copying or ingesting it into a data store**. Each connector is backed by a **first-party MCP server**; the request is authenticated with the **end user's own IAM permissions or OAuth 2.1 credentials**, and the agent formulates SQL and invokes the connector's MCP tools against the live database. Attaching a connector in this mode **automatically enables Knowledge Catalog** on the app's Assistant tab, giving the root agent read-only tools to search data assets and pull back tables, schemas, business glossary terms and enriched metadata. Three things change for coverage: there is **no data store artifact to inventory** — the old "what did this agent ingest" question no longer answers "what can this agent read"; the reachable data set is now **per-user and dynamic**, so entitlement review has to be evaluated against each caller rather than the app; and **Knowledge Catalog turns on implicitly**, adding a metadata-discovery surface the admin did not explicitly enable. Preview across AlloyDB for PostgreSQL, BigQuery, Cloud SQL and Spanner. AISPM must discover federated-mode connectors, their backing MCP servers, the databases they reach and the Knowledge Catalog enablement state

findings.title: Copilot Studio extract node — model-selectable document parsing inside workflows
findings.description: A new workflow node processes invoices, contracts, receipts, bank statements, reports and financial statements across PDF, Word, Excel and PowerPoint, returning named values and tables as dynamic content for later steps. The extraction schema can be inferred from an uploaded sample document, chosen from a template, or defined by hand, and the **model powering extraction is selected by the maker** from a dropdown. For coverage this is a new data-transformation point where unstructured documents — frequently the most sensitive artifacts in a tenant — are read by an LLM and emitted as structured tokens that flow onward into Dataverse records, approvals, emails and Teams messages. The document itself arrives from a trigger (a mailbox attachment, a SharePoint library), so the node is a standing conduit from inbound untrusted files into the workflow's execution context — an indirect prompt injection path worth AIRT attention as well. AISPM should inventory extract nodes, their configured input source, selected model and output field schema

findings.title: Copilot Studio content safety test method — a new configurable guardrail threshold surface in agent evaluation
findings.description: Agent evaluation gained a **content safety** test method, added separately per content type across hatefulness/unfairness, sexual content, violence and self-harm. Each is configured with a **severity threshold on a 0–7 scale, where 0 is strictest and 7 is the most permissive and allows graphic or extreme content to pass**. This is a per-agent, maker-controlled safety configuration — meaning the threshold a given agent is validated against is now an inventoried posture attribute, and an agent whose content-safety tests are set to a permissive level (or absent entirely) is a measurably weaker configuration than its neighbour. Microsoft explicitly warns the evaluations "don't guarantee that an agent is safe or appropriate for every scenario." AISPM should capture the configured thresholds per agent and flag permissive or missing content-safety evaluation as a violation rule

findings.title: AgentCore Gateway private certificate authority support for targets
findings.description: AgentCore Gateway now accepts TLS server certificates signed by **private CAs** on MCP server, OpenAPI and HTTP proxy (passthrough) targets. Previously the gateway trusted only publicly-issued certificates, which in practice forced private targets behind an Application Load Balancer. An operator now registers a PEM-encoded CA certificate held in **Amazon S3 or AWS Secrets Manager** as the trust anchor, and the gateway connects **directly to private endpoints inside the customer VPC powered by Amazon VPC Lattice**. The coverage consequence is that AgentCore agents can now reach internal, non-internet-facing services with no load balancer in the path — removing the network chokepoint that previously made that egress observable, and introducing two new inventory attributes per target: the trust-anchor location (an S3 object or a Secrets Manager secret) and the VPC Lattice private endpoint it authorises. AISPM should enumerate gateway targets using a private CA and map the internal services each one reaches

findings.title: Codex CLI MCP authentication surfaces — OAuth client secrets and WebSocket bearer tokens
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.158.0 (2026-09-28) added **OAuth client-secret support for MCP servers** and **WebSocket bearer-token authentication**, and 0.160.1 (2026-10-05) fixed preservation of Windows environment variables for remote MCP servers. Together these mean a developer's local Codex configuration now holds long-lived credentials for remote MCP servers, authenticates over WebSocket transports, and sources secrets from the Windows environment. ENDPOINT must extend Codex MCP discovery to capture the authentication method per server (OAuth client secret vs. bearer token vs. none), the transport, and whether credentials are inlined in config or drawn from environment variables

findings.title: OpenAI API key governance controls at organization and project level
findings.description: OpenAI added an **API Key Governance** section in platform settings (2026-09-15) letting organization and project administrators restrict which key types may be created — **service-account keys only, user-owned project keys only, or no new keys at all** — with organization-level restrictions always taking precedence over project settings, and existing keys unaffected. A companion change (2026-09-10) lets administrators enforce a **maximum API key lifetime**, requiring new keys to expire within a configured limit. These are new tenant posture attributes on a primary-tier platform: an organization permitting user-owned keys with no lifetime cap is materially weaker than one restricted to expiring service-account keys, and the "existing keys unaffected" carve-out means a restriction can be in force while long-lived legacy keys remain valid behind it. AISPM should read the governance setting at both levels and flag organizations with unrestricted or unexpiring key issuance

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise resource-level IAM for apps and data stores
findings.description: Administrators can now grant **Gemini Enterprise Admin, Viewer or User roles on an individual app or data store** rather than across the whole Google Cloud project, and can build custom project-level roles for restricted administrators, viewers and end users. Until now, a project-level grant applied uniformly to every Gemini Enterprise app and data store in the project — so entitlement could be reasoned about at project granularity. It no longer can: effective access is the union of project-level and per-resource bindings, and the per-resource grants are configurable through the console, gcloud **and the REST API**. AISPM's Gemini Enterprise entitlement model must be re-derived per app and per data store, and flag resources whose resource-level bindings widen access beyond the project grant

findings.title: Perplexity Decisions API and Agent API document/image tooling
findings.description: Perplexity shipped a **Decisions API** at `POST https://api.perplexity.ai/v1/decisions`, powered by a dedicated model (`pplx-decider-v1-27b`) that returns a **probability distribution over a fixed answer set** instead of generated text — supporting yes/no, pick-one-of-N, and rubric-score question types over text, JSON or images. This is the second vendor in two scans to ship a constrained-decision endpoint (OpenAI's Decisions API was reported 2026-10-01), confirming a **cross-vendor pattern: model-driven control flow that routes an agent's next action and produces no inspectable text output to monitor**. Alongside it, the Agent API gained **native document ingestion** (`input_file` accepting PDF/DOC/DOCX/TXT/RTF, inline or by public HTTPS URL — note that a public URL means Perplexity fetches the document server-side) and a new **`image_search`** tool. AISPM should add the decisions endpoint and the new Agent API tools to the Perplexity inventory and treat decision calls as unmonitored control-flow points; AIDR needs the document-ingestion path as a data-egress activity type

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI) — primary
details: **Agents API** — a managed agent runtime distinct from the Responses API. Object model is **Agent** (model, instructions, tools, MCP servers), **Environment** (sandbox), **Session** (durable, server-retained state across turns) and **Events/items**. Sessions are created at `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/agents/sessions` behind the `OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1` header. Supports **subagent delegation** (up to 4 concurrent in documented examples), MCP servers over HTTP transport, web search, code execution, file editing and command execution. OpenAI manages orchestration, context compaction and recovery. US-only data residency; **Zero Data Retention is not supported, even with self-hosted sandboxes**. Entered public beta 2026-09-10 and was not caught by prior scans. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/overview

**Computer use in the Agents API** (2026-09-29) — agents drive a browser in an **OpenAI-hosted environment**, with per-origin approval and in-band credential collection. Source: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog

**Dots** (2026-09-29) — always-on autonomous agents in ChatGPT, powered by GPT-6 Astra. Each dot has **its own cloud computer and browser**, runs while the user is offline, reaches 4,000+ apps through plugins, and delegates to background subagents. Off by default; enabled per workspace by an administrator. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots

**Local computer access for dots and Work Cloud** — a cloud-orchestrated agent executing on the user's own machine, gated by a new **Agent Security** admin surface. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-local-access

**ChatGPT Space** (2026-09-29) — collaborative pages where agents are invoked inline, in comments and via slash commands. New entity set: Spaces, Members, Agents, Connectors, Files. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/space/agents

**Decisions API** (2026-09-29) — a new constrained-output decision endpoint backed by GPT-6 Luna; limited preview, GA announced on the OpenAI API and Microsoft Foundry. Source: https://openai.com/index/devday-2026-recap/

findings.title: OpenAI Agents API — a managed agent runtime with server-held sessions, sandbox environments and subagents
findings.description: OpenAI now runs the agent loop itself rather than leaving orchestration to the customer's code. Four new entity types enter the inventory — **Agent** (model + instructions + tools + attached MCP servers), **Environment** (an execution sandbox, OpenAI-hosted or self-hosted), **Session** (a *durable* agent instance whose conversation state, compaction and recovery are retained server-side by OpenAI), and **Events/items**. Agents may attach arbitrary **remote MCP servers over HTTP**, run **code execution, file editing and shell commands** inside the environment, and **delegate to subagents**, so one inventoried agent can fan out into a tree of executions the customer never registered. Two properties make this materially riskier than the Responses API surface Zenity already maps: session state is a **new OpenAI-side data store** that holds full conversation history, and **Zero Data Retention is not supported at all — even when the customer supplies their own sandbox**, so ZDR-contracted enterprises silently lose that guarantee the moment a team adopts the Agents API. Data residency is US-only. This went to public beta on 2026-09-10 and was missed for three weeks. AISPM must discover Agents, Environments and Sessions as first-class resources, enumerate each agent's MCP server attachments and tool grants, and flag ZDR-contracted tenants with Agents API usage

findings.title: Computer use in the Agents API — end-user passwords and verification codes are submitted into an OpenAI-hosted browser, and approval is per-origin, not per-action
findings.description: The Agents API now runs a full browser inside an OpenAI-controlled environment. Two documented properties are direct attack surface. First, **approval granularity is the origin, not the action**: a `computer_use_approval_request` of type `browser_origin_access` is raised once per new origin, and OpenAI's own documentation states that origin approval "does not enforce confirmation before individual actions" — so a single approval of a trusted domain authorises every subsequent purchase, deletion or data export the agent performs there, which is precisely the payoff an indirect prompt injection on that page is reaching for. Second, **the credential path is in-band**: for authenticated tasks the hosted browser raises a `browser_authentication` request and the application collects the user's email, password and verification codes and submits them through the **session events endpoint** — live human credentials and OTPs flowing into an OpenAI-hosted browser session. Passkeys and QR sign-in are not supported, which pushes tenants toward the weaker shared-secret path. Screenshots of authenticated pages are returned to the application and OpenAI warns they must be kept out of logs. AIRT should build injection and over-approval scenarios against origin-scoped consent; AISPM should inventory which agents carry the `computer_use` tool with the `openai_hosted` environment and treat them as credential-handling systems

findings.title: OpenAI Dots — always-on autonomous agents with their own cloud computer, 4,000+ app reach and background subagents
findings.description: Dots, announced at DevDay on 2026-09-29, are persistent agents that **keep working after the user logs off**. Each dot is powered by GPT-6 Astra and is provisioned with **its own cloud computer and browser**, can act across **4,000+ apps via plugins already connected to the account**, and spawns **background subagents** to run tasks in parallel. Governance is a layered custom-rules model — read-only background research, four levels of Custom Rules, mandatory human takeover for passwords and money transfers, and an automatic pre-action auto-review — all of which are **per-dot configuration that an enterprise has no inventory of today**. Dots are off by default and enabled by a workspace administrator, which makes enablement state itself a posture signal. This is a new non-human identity class on the OpenAI surface: long-lived, self-directed, inheriting the user's full connector grants, and executing with no human in the session. AISPM must inventory dots per workspace, their Custom Rules level, their enabled plugin/connector reach, and flag dots whose inherited connector scope exceeds their owner's need; AIDR needs dot activity as a distinct, user-absent activity type

findings.title: Local computer access for dots and Work Cloud — OpenAI-orchestrated agents executing on employee machines, with audit split across two incompatible pipelines
findings.description: A new **"Allow local computer access"** permission lets a cloud-orchestrated dot or Work task execute on the user's own machine: running local repositories and developer tools, driving **desktop applications and the local browser**, and implementing changes and builds against local files. This is a managed-endpoint agent, governed through a new **Agent Security** admin surface with a Global baseline and per-environment overrides (approval policies and web search mode are Global-only and cannot be overridden). It requires ChatGPT desktop 26.929+. The audit story has documented holes Zenity should treat as coverage requirements rather than assurances: **local execution telemetry only leaves via OpenTelemetry export to the customer's own collector**, while **cloud orchestration records go to the Compliance API** — the two never meet, and **cloud OTel events do not reach legacy collectors**. OpenAI further documents that **MCP hooks do not provide complete audit trails** and that callback failures (timeouts, malformed responses) **can occur without blocking the action**, i.e. the agent proceeds while the control plane is blind. A `enforce_residency` cloud policy disables the feature, and it is unavailable for FedRAMP, EKM and UAE-residency workspaces. ENDPOINT must detect the desktop local executor and its permission state; AIDR must correlate the OTel local stream against Compliance API cloud records to find actions that executed with no corresponding audit record

findings.title: ChatGPT Space — a collaborative document surface with embedded agents and connector reach
findings.description: Space introduces shared pages where agents are invoked inline (`@ChatGPT`, `@dot`), from comments, from a conversation sidebar and through slash commands. It brings a new entity set — **Spaces, Members (with differing permission levels), Agents including custom dots, Connectors, and Files** — and the agents available inside a Space inherit whatever tools the workspace has enabled. The security-relevant shape is a **multi-tenant collaborative container where an agent reads shared member content and reaches enterprise connectors**: content pasted into a Space by one member becomes agent-readable context for every agent invoked there, which is both a data-boundary question and an indirect prompt injection path. AISPM should inventory Spaces, their membership and permission levels, which agents and connectors are reachable from each, and flag Spaces whose connector reach crosses data-classification boundaries

findings.title: OpenAI Decisions API — a new constrained-choice endpoint that routes agent control flow
findings.description: The Decisions API, introduced at DevDay on 2026-09-29, lets an application hand a narrow repetitive choice to GPT-6 Luna: the caller supplies context as text or images plus a **fixed set of predefined answers**, and the model selects among them. It is explicitly positioned for classifying content, routing requests, and **choosing an agent's next action** — which makes it a control-flow component, not a content-generation one, and therefore an unmonitored decision point inside agent pipelines Zenity otherwise maps. It is distinct from Structured Outputs (which constrains response *shape*, not the answer set). Announced GA on the OpenAI API and **Microsoft Foundry**, currently limited preview with no public endpoint schema yet; AISPM should add it to the OpenAI API inventory now and revisit when the reference publishes, since a Foundry-side surface means it will also appear on a Microsoft primary-tier platform

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **Codex CLI 0.158.0 (2026-09-28) adds OAuth client-secret storage and bearer-token

findings.title: Anthropic advisor tool — an undeclared, model-initiated transcript egress to a second model
findings.description: A new server-side tool (`advisor_20260301`) lets any Claude request nominate a second "advisor" model that, on the executor's own initiative, receives the **entire conversation transcript including the system prompt, all tool definitions, every prior turn and every tool result**. The calling application never sees what was sent — `server_tool_use.input` is always empty and the server assembles the advisor's view itself. `max_uses` defaults to **unlimited**, so a single request can trigger an unbounded number of these passes. AIDR needs a new activity type for advisor invocations and must treat the `advisor` tool's presence in a `tools` array as a full-context data flow to a second model, distinct from the tool calls it already tracks

findings.title: Advisor results are encrypted on every current model — an opaque model-to-model channel
findings.description: On Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Fable 5 and Mythos 5, the advisor returns `advisor_redacted_result` with `encrypted_content`, and those models as executors *cannot* be paired with a plaintext advisor — Anthropic states "the advice text isn't readable in the response." Strategic guidance therefore reaches the executor and steers its subsequent tool calls through a channel neither the customer nor any content inspector can read. This is a prompt-injection amplification path worth red-teaming: content injected into the transcript reaches the advisor, whose (invisible) response then redirects the executor. AIRT should build probes that measure executor behaviour change across advisor-on/advisor-off runs, since inspecting the advice directly is not possible. A second variant exists on Claude Managed Agents where advice is delivered as **thread events** rather than result blocks, so detectors keyed on the block type miss it

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise resource-level IAM on apps and data stores
findings.description: Gemini Enterprise apps and data stores are now first-class IAM resource scopes, managed through `getIamPolicy` / `setIamPolicy` on the app itself, with `roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser` bound per-app, alongside new custom project-level roles for restricted administrators, viewers and end users. Two behaviours make this a detection requirement rather than a nicety. First, **project-level IAM takes precedence over app-level policy** — a principal holding Gemini Enterprise User at the project level reaches *every* app regardless of app-level bindings, so genuinely restricting a user requires swapping them to the new **Gemini Enterprise Restricted User** role and then granting per-app. Second, `setIamPolicy` **replaces** the entire policy, so a partial write silently strips bindings. AISPM must fetch per-resource IAM policy on each app and data store, add the restricted-{administrator,viewer,user} personas to its inventory, and flag the toxic combination of a project-level Gemini Enterprise User grant coexisting with app-level restrictions that it silently defeats

findings.title: Codex CLI stores MCP OAuth client secrets and exposes bearer-authenticated exec-server WebSockets
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.158.0 adds `codex mcp add --oauth-client-id <id> --oauth-client-secret <secret>`, which **persists a pre-registered OAuth client secret into the Codex server configuration** on the developer workstation (the secret is redacted in debug output and kept out of authorization URLs and persisted token records, but the config file itself now holds it). The same release adds bearer-token authentication to direct exec-server WebSocket connections, extended to app-server configured connections. ENDPOINT needs to inventory this new credential material in the Codex config and to recognise the exec-server WebSocket as a locally-listening, token-authenticated command-execution surface
